brief.headline: Push for ₹32.69 L/yr savings by matching our best price, and offer faster payment for a further 4.38% cut — but line up a second source first because they're 76% of our laminates.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹290.00/KG — the price Shrinath Roto Pack already gives us — across the three biggest SKUs
priceAsk.target: ₹290.00/KG and close the ₹32.69 L annual gap
priceAsk.basis: The open market for pharma/ORS sachets is ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg) and we already pay ₹290.00/KG to Shrinath Roto Pack. GEEP's prices on the top three SKUs — ₹294.03, ₹308.30, ₹294.57 — sit at the top of fair band and above our own best, costing us ₹32.69 L extra every year.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (at 15 days instead of 30) in return for a 4.38% price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster ties up ₹1.16 Cr more of our cash, but their borrowing costs them about 4.38% — so early payment is worth roughly that rate to them, and we turn trapped cash into a price win.

brief.financialLeverage: GEEP sells ₹291.36 Cr a year and keeps only 1.1% as profit, so they have little room to absorb a big price cut without it hurting them. But their cash is stuck for 81 days — longer than similar firms at 46 days — which means cash is tight for them and faster payment has real value. We're 9.72% of everything they sell (₹28.31 Cr out of ₹291.36 Cr), so we're a customer they want to keep. The rating is CRISIL BB+ / Stable, but the agency did it without their help, and they've had GST and EPF payment delays plus pending legal cases, so treat their health as uncertain. Push hard on matching our best price and trade faster payment for a rate cut, but keep a second source ready because 76% of our laminates come from them and we can't risk losing supply.

evidence.point: We pay ₹32.69 L/yr more than the best price we already get
Our best laminate price today is ₹290.00/KG from Shrinath Roto Pack

Paying 15 days faster ties up ₹1.16 Cr of our cash and is worth about 4.38% to them

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter (already a tiny FDC supplier) — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant — both film substrate and conversion; can second-source GEEP at scale

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter — pharma blister/sachet laminates; strong second-source for GEEP

risks: They're 76% of our laminates spend (₹28.31 Cr) — pushing too hard without a qualified backup could leave us short if they walk or stumble.
The CRISIL BB+ rating was done without their cooperation, and they have GST filing delays, EPF payment delays and pending legal cases — so their real financial health is uncertain.

They keep only 1.1% profit, so a steep price cut could squeeze them too far and hurt our supply; frame the ask as matching our best price (not a deep discount) and trade payment speed for rate relief.
Their cash is stuck for 81 days vs peers at 46 days, so they need liquidity — use faster payment as the sweetener, not just a demand.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: You're a key partner — nearly 10% of your sales — and we want to keep growing together, but we need to talk about three things: matching the ₹290/kg we already pay elsewhere, a rate cut if we pay you faster, and making sure we have a second source lined up so both of us stay secure.
